title: Udaipur - The City of Lakes and Royal Heritage
content:
Udaipur

Udaipur, also known as the “City of Lakes”, is one of the most beautiful travel destinations in India. Located in the heart of Rajasthan and surrounded by the Aravalli Hills, this royal city is famous for its serene lakes, grand palaces, historic temples, colorful streets, and rich culture. Udaipur is often called the “Venice of the East” because of its romantic feel and breathtaking landscapes, making it a favorite destination for couples, families, and history lovers alike.

The most popular attraction in Udaipur is the City Palace, a stunning palace complex that reflects the grandeur of the Rajput era. Just nearby, the sparkling Lake Pichola offers mesmerizing views of the city, especially during a boat ride at sunset. Another must-visit is the Jagdish Temple, a beautiful Hindu temple with intricate carvings that display the city’s artistic heritage. For those who love nature, Fateh Sagar Lake is a peaceful spot to enjoy scenic beauty, while the historic Saheliyon Ki Bari garden with fountains and lotus pools adds to Udaipur’s charm. The majestic Jag Mandir, built on an island in Lake Pichola, is another highlight that gives visitors a royal experience.

The best time to visit Udaipur is between October and March, when the weather is pleasant for sightseeing. A trip to Udaipur is incomplete without shopping in its bustling bazaars for traditional handicrafts, jewelry, paintings, and Rajasthani fabrics. Food lovers can also enjoy authentic Rajasthani delicacies like dal bati churma and gatte ki sabzi, which add to the cultural experience.

With its perfect blend of history, architecture, romance, and natural beauty, Udaipur truly captures the heart of every traveler. Whether you’re planning a short trip or a long holiday, Udaipur promises unforgettable memories and an experience of Rajasthan’s royal lifestyle. Click here for Udaipur Packages

Top Attractions in Udaipur

1. City Palace, Udaipur: A Glimpse into Royal Grandeur

 

Overlooking the serene Lake Pichola, the City Palace of Udaipur is one of Rajasthan’s most iconic landmarks. Built over centuries by the Mewar dynasty, this magnificent palace complex blends Rajasthani and Mughal architecture, featuring grand courtyards, intricate balconies, and stunning views.

Inside, the palace showcases a rich collection of art, mirror work, marble carvings, and royal artifacts. Highlights include the Sheesh Mahal, Badi Mahal, and the Crystal Gallery, each offering a unique glimpse into royal life.

Don’t miss the City Palace Museum and the evening light and sound show, which beautifully narrates Udaipur’s regal history. A visit here is like stepping into a royal past - majestic, colorful, and unforgettable.

Entrance Info:

Main Entrance: Badi Pol (main gate) or Tripolia Gate

Timings: 9:30 AM – 5:30 PM (daily)

Entry Fee: Adults: ₹300, Children (5–18 years): ₹100 & Camera: ₹250 (approx.) Museum Combo tickets also available

 

2. Lake Pichola: The Sparkling Heart of Udaipur

 

Lake Pichola is one of Udaipur’s most iconic and picturesque attractions. Surrounded by majestic hills, historic palaces, and ghats, this artificial freshwater lake was created in the 14th century and later expanded by Maharana Udai Singh II when he founded the city.

The lake is best known for its scenic boat rides, which offer stunning views of the City Palace, Jag Mandir, and the world-famous Taj Lake Palace - a white marble marvel that seems to float in the middle of the water.

Sunrise and sunset over Lake Pichola are truly magical, casting golden reflections on its calm surface. Whether you're exploring from the shore or gliding across by boat, the lake captures the romantic essence of Udaipur and is a must-visit for every traveler.
 

3. Jag Mandir: The Island of Tranquility and Royal Charm

 

Nestled in the serene waters of Lake Pichola, Jag Mandir is a beautiful 17th-century palace built on an island. Often called the "Lake Garden Palace," it was constructed by the Mewar rulers as a summer retreat and a place of refuge for royal guests - including Prince Khurram, who later became Emperor Shah Jahan.

The palace features elegant Mughal and Rajput architecture, with stunning marble chhatris, courtyards, and gardens surrounded by calm waters. The most iconic sight is the row of marble elephants standing guard at the entrance, welcoming visitors with grandeur.

Today, Jag Mandir is a peaceful escape from the city’s bustle - perfect for a boat ride stop, a lakeside lunch, or simply soaking in the royal ambiance with panoramic views of Udaipur.

Access Info:

How to Reach: Only accessible by boat from City Palace jetty (Rameshwar Ghat)

Boat Ride Timings: 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM Often included in Lake Pichola boat ride packages

Entry Fee: Included in boat ride (No separate ticket)

 

4. Fateh Sagar Lake: Udaipur’s Blue Gem

 

Located in the northern part of Udaipur, Fateh Sagar Lake is a tranquil and scenic artificial lake surrounded by the Aravalli hills. Built in the 17th century and later rebuilt by Maharana Fateh Singh, it’s known as the “second major lake” of the city, after Lake Pichola.

The lake is divided into three islands, the most popular being Nehru Park - a lush garden island with a boat-shaped café and scenic walking paths. Another island houses a solar observatory, one of the few in Asia.

With its clean blue waters, cool breeze, and picturesque backdrop, Fateh Sagar is perfect for boat rides, evening walks, and sunset views. It’s a favorite spot among locals and tourists alike for a peaceful escape within the city.

  • Entry Fee: Free
  • Boat Ride Cost: ₹30 - ₹400 depending on boat type and duration
  • Promenade Access: Free & open throughout the day
     

5. Saheliyon ki Bari


 

Tucked away in the northern part of Udaipur, Saheliyon Ki Bari is a beautifully landscaped garden built in the early 18th century by Maharana Sangram Singh for the royal ladies of the court. Designed as a peaceful retreat, it was meant to be a gift for the queen and her entourage of maids — a place where they could relax, away from palace politics.

The garden features lush green lawns, marble pavilions, lotus pools, and ornate fountains, all surrounded by a sense of calm and symmetry. The star attraction is the rain fountains, imported from England, that still work beautifully today, offering a cool, misty escape from the desert heat.

Timings: 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM, daily
Entry Fee: Adults: ₹10 – ₹20, Foreigners: ₹50 – ₹100 (prices may vary slightly)

 

6. Bagore Ki Haveli: A Cultural Window into Royal Rajasthan

 

Located right on the banks of Lake Pichola, near Gangaur Ghat, Bagore Ki Haveli is an 18th-century mansion built by Amar Chand Badwa, the Prime Minister of Mewar. Today, it stands as a beautifully restored museum and cultural hub that offers a glimpse into the lavish lifestyle of Rajput nobles.

The haveli features over 100 rooms with stunning intricate mirror work, colorful glass windows, antique furniture, costumes, and traditional artworks. Each section narrates a different aspect of Rajasthani culture - from royal quarters to weapon displays and musical instruments.

One of the major highlights is the Dharohar Dance Show, held every evening in the courtyard. This vibrant performance showcases folk dances, puppetry, and music from across Rajasthan, making it a cultural experience you shouldn't miss.

Timings

  • Museum: 9:30 AM – 5:30 PM (daily)
  • Dharohar Dance Show: 7:00 PM – 8:00 PM

Entry Fee

Museum:

  • Indians: ₹60–₹100
  • Foreigners: ₹100–₹150
  • Camera Fee: ₹50 (approx.)

Dance Show:

  • Adults: ₹90–₹150
  • Children: ₹45–₹75 (Prices may vary slightly)
     

7. Jagdish Temple: Udaipur’s Spiritual Landmark

 

Located just a short walk from the City Palace, Jagdish Temple is one of Udaipur’s most iconic and sacred sites. Built in 1651 by Maharana Jagat Singh, this grand Indo-Aryan style temple is dedicated to Lord Vishnu, worshipped here as Jagannath, the preserver of the universe.

The temple stands tall with intricately carved pillars, beautifully sculpted ceilings, and detailed stonework, reflecting the artistry of Mewar’s golden age. As you climb the steep flight of marble steps, you're welcomed by a majestic black stone idol of Lord Vishnu and smaller shrines dedicated to Shiva, Ganesh, Surya, and Shakti.

A visit during morning or evening aarti (ritual prayer) fills the temple with the sound of bells, chants, and spiritual energy - a truly serene experience.

Timings: 4:30 AM to 1:00 PM & 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM (Open daily)

Entry Fee: Free
